'''Isabel Fernández Delgado''' (born 1979){{r|gadea}} is a Spanish mathematician specializing in [[geometric analysis]].{{r|rsme}} She is university professor of applied mathematics at the [[University of Seville]],{{r|prisma}} and an editor-in-chief of the ''Revista Matemática Iberoamericana''.{{r|rmi}}

==Education and career==
Fernández was born in [[Linares, Jaén]],{{r|rsme}} in 1979.{{r|gadea}}
She received a [[licenciate]] in mathematics from the [[University of Granada]] in 2002.{{r|gadea}} She completed her Ph.D. there in 2006 with the dissertation ''Superficies maximales con singularidades aisladas'' supervised by Francisco López Fernández.{{r|mg}}

After short-term positions at the [[University of Murcia]] and the [[University of Extremadura]], she obtained an assistant professor position at the University of Seville in 2007. In 2010 she was promoted to ''profesora titular'', the equivalent of an associate professor.{{r|rsme}} Her current title is ''profesora titular de universidad'' (university professor).{{r|prisma}}

==Recognition==
Fernández was an invited speaker at the 2010 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].
The Royal Seville Academy of Sciences and Royal Cavalry Master of Seville gave Fernández their 2012 Young Researcher Prize.{{r|3j}}
